findings.description: The instance user-data embeds an AWS access key ID and secret access key in plaintext. User-data is retrievable by principals with instance describe access and the values are also committed to IaC source, exposing reusable credentials.
No metadata_options configuration requires IMDSv2 tokens. This leaves IMDSv1 available, so an SSRF flaw on the instance could be used to retrieve instance metadata and any role credentials.
The instance does not configure an encrypted root_block_device. Consequently, root-volume encryption depends on AMI and account defaults rather than being enforced by this workload configuration.
The EBS volume has no encrypted = true setting or KMS key. Its data may therefore be created unencrypted when account-level default EBS encryption is not enabled.
This snapshot is created from a volume whose encryption is not enforced. EBS snapshots inherit the source volume's encryption state, so this can preserve the volume's data without encryption at rest.
TCP/22 is allowed from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing remote administration to every internet host. This permits internet-wide scanning and password/key-authentication attacks against the instance.
The egress rule permits all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0. A compromised web host can use this unrestricted path for command-and-control communications or data exfiltration.
The flow-log bucket has no server-side encryption configuration. Sensitive network-flow records can be stored without encryption at rest unless an external account-level default happens to supply it.
